html:
French Fezzan was the desert south west of Libya, run by a French military government from 1943 until Libya became independent in 1951.

The Fezzan is a land of oases and sand seas, with Sabha as its main town. During the Second World War, Free French forces under General Leclerc struck north from Chad into the Italian colony. By early 1943 they held the Fezzan, while the British took the north; see Italian Libya.

After the war Libya was split in three: France held the Fezzan, and Britain held Tripolitania and Cyrenaica. France hoped to keep the Fezzan as a link between its Saharan lands. The United Nations decided instead that Libya should be one free country, and in 1951 the Fezzan joined the Kingdom of Libya.
sum: French Fezzan was the desert south west of Libya, run by a French military government from 1943 until Libya became independent in 1951.
